candidate.derivedAnswer: B: There are finitely many, and each is equally likely
candidate.answerReason: A classical probability model has finitely many sample points, all equally likely. This is exactly option B.

methods.label: Classical-model conditions
methods.explanation: The classical probability model requires finitely many sample points, each equally likely. Without equal likelihood, the count ratio \(m/n\), where \(m\) is the favorable count and \(n>0\) is the total count, cannot be applied directly. Therefore the answer is B.
methods.levelReason: Uses only the defining conditions of the classical probability model and elementary sample-space vocabulary.
